title: Compounded drug preparation label and compounding pharmacy telephone line under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21
subtopic: Compounded preparation label and pharmacist telephone line
rule_summary: The fourth paragraph of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 provides that the labeling provisions of the section shall apply to the compounding and dispensing of drugs on the oral, electronic or written prescription of a licensed and registered prescriber under section 9, and that all drug preparations compounded, made or formulated by a pharmacy licensed by the board of registration in pharmacy shall have affixed to their container by the compounding pharmacy a label notifying prescribed users and practitioners that the drug is either a sterile or non-sterile compounded drug preparation. Under the fifth paragraph, all pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding and licensed under sections 39G to 39I, inclusive, of chapter 112 shall provide a telephone number to foster communication between patients in the commonwealth and a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records. The phone shall be staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week, and the phone number shall be affixed to the drug's container, alongside the label notifying prescribed users and practitioners of the fact that the drug is a compounded drug preparation. The fifth paragraph shall not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed pursuant to section 39I of chapter 112 if the sterile drug preparation compounded by such pharmacy is to be administered to an individual admitted as an inpatient within the same hospital.
exam_relevance: Tests the two separate compounded-preparation duties in s. 21: the label that reaches every preparation compounded, made or formulated by a Board-licensed pharmacy, and the staffed pharmacist telephone line that reaches only pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding and licensed under c. 112, ss. 39G to 39I, with an inpatient exception written into the telephone paragraph alone.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws c. 94C
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21, fourth and fifth paragraphs

numeric_facts.fact: minimum staffing of the compounding pharmacy telephone line
numeric_facts.conditions: pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding and licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 39G to 39I, inclusive; the phone is also to be staffed during regular hours of operation every day

exceptions: The telephone paragraph shall not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed pursuant to M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39I if the sterile drug preparation compounded by such pharmacy is to be administered to an individual admitted as an inpatient within the same hospital.
common_confusions: The compounded drug preparation label reaches all drug preparations compounded, made or formulated by a pharmacy licensed by the Board, not only sterile or complex non-sterile preparations.
The telephone line is owed by pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding and licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 39G to 39I, inclusive; the label duty is not limited in that way.
The inpatient exception is written into the telephone paragraph only; the text states no exception to the compounded drug preparation label.

The telephone line must connect patients with a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records, staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week.
verification_notes: Read in full on 2026-09-16 in the text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 on malegislature.gov; the compounded drug preparation provisions are the second sentence of the fourth paragraph and the whole of the fifth paragraph.
